questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A body of mass 'm' attached at the end of a string is just completing the loop in a vertical circle. The apparent weight of the body at the lowest point in its path is
($g$ = gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution:
For a body to just complete a vertical circle, the tension in the string at the highest point is zero.

$T_H + mg = \dfrac{m v_H^2}{r} \Rightarrow v_H = \sqrt{gr}$

By conservation of mechanical energy between the highest and lowest points:

$\dfrac{1}{2} m v_L^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_H^2 + mg(2r)$

$v_L^2 = v_H^2 + 4gr = gr + 4gr = 5gr$

At the lowest point, the net force towards the center provides the centripetal acceleration:

$T_L - mg = \dfrac{m v_L^2}{r}$

$T_L = mg + \dfrac{m(5gr)}{r} = mg + 5mg = 6mg$

The apparent weight of the body is equal to the tension in the string at that point, which is $6$ mg.

Answer: $6\,mg$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The spring is initially in unstretched condition. It is first stretched by a length '$x$' and the work done is $W_1$. Then again it is stretched by further length '$x$' when the work done is $W_2$. The value of $W_2$ is given by
questions.solution:
Work done in stretching a spring from its natural length to an extension $x$ is given by $W_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^2$.

When the spring is further stretched by a length $x$, the total extension becomes $2x$.

Total work done from the natural length to an extension $2x$ is $W = \dfrac{1}{2}k(2x)^2 = 4 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}kx^2\right) = 4W_1$.

Work done in the second step is $W_2 = W - W_1 = 4W_1 - W_1 = 3W_1$.

Answer: $3W_1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass 1kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\vec{F} = (t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j})\ \text{N}$ where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are the unit vectors along x and y axis. The power developed by the above force at time $t = 2\ \text{s}$ will be (in watt)
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{F} = t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j}$ and $m = 1\ \text{kg}$.

Acceleration $\vec{a} = \dfrac{\vec{F}}{m} = t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j}$

Velocity $\vec{v} = \int \vec{a} dt = \dfrac{t^2}{2}\hat{i} + t^3\hat{j}$ (since the body begins to move from rest, $\vec{v}(0) = 0$).

At $t = 2\ \text{s}$:

$\vec{F} = 2\hat{i} + 3(2)^2\hat{j} = 2\hat{i} + 12\hat{j}$

$\vec{v} = \dfrac{2^2}{2}\hat{i} + (2)^3\hat{j} = 2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j}$

Power $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = (2\hat{i} + 12\hat{j}) \cdot (2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j})$

$P = (2 \times 2) + (12 \times 8) = 4 + 96 = 100\ \text{W}$

Answer: $100$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass 'm' moving on a frictionless horizontal surface collides with a spring of spring constant 'K' and compresses it through a distance 'x'. The maximum momentum of the block after collision is
questions.solution:
By the principle of conservation of mechanical energy, the maximum kinetic energy of the block is equal to the maximum potential energy stored in the spring at maximum compression.

$\dfrac{p^2}{2m} = \dfrac{1}{2} K x^2$

$p^2 = m K x^2$

$p = \sqrt{m K} x$

The maximum momentum of the block after the collision is equal in magnitude to its initial momentum, which is $\sqrt{m K} x$.

Answer: $\sqrt{\text{km}}\ x$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bucket containing water is revolved in vertical circle of radius r. To prevent the water from falling down, the period of revolution required is ($g$ = gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution:
At the highest point of the vertical circle, the forces acting on the water are its weight $mg$ downwards and the normal reaction $N$ from the bucket downwards.

The necessary centripetal force is provided by these forces:

$mg + N = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$

To prevent the water from falling down, the normal reaction must be greater than or equal to zero (N \ge 0$). The minimum speed $v$ is obtained when $N = 0$:

$mg = $\dfrac{mv^2}{r} \Rightarrow$v = $\sqrt{rg}

The angular velocity \omega$ corresponding to this minimum speed is:

$\omega = \dfrac{v}{r} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{r}}$

The maximum period of revolution $T$ required to prevent the water from falling is:

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{r}{g}}$

Answer: $2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{r}{g}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A stone of mass ' m ' kg is tied to a string of length ' L ' m and moved in a vertical circle of radius 49 cm in a vertical plane. If it completes 30 revolutions per minute, the tension in the string when it is at the lowermost point is nearly
[Take $\pi^2=10$ and acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ]
questions.solution:
The mass is $m$ kg, with string length (radius) $L = 0.49\text{ m}$, and rotational frequency $f = 0.5\text{ rps}$. Angular velocity is $\omega = 2\pi f = \pi\text{ rad/s}$.

Centripetal acceleration becomes $a_c = \omega^2 L = (\pi)^2 (0.49) = 10 \times 0.49 = 4.9\text{ m/s}^2$.

At the lowermost point, the net centripetal force satisfies $T - mg = ma_c$. Solving yields the tension: $T = m(g + a_c) = m(10 + 4.9) = 14.9m\text{ N}$.

This gives $T \approx 15m\text{ N}$, corresponding to option D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A constant force $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ newton has a displacement $\vec{r}=2 \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}-3 \hat{k}$ metre in 2 second. The work done and the power are respectively
questions.solution:
The work done by a constant force is computed using the dot product of force and displacement vectors. Given $\overrightarrow{F} = 3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j} - \hat{k}\, \text{N}$ and $\overrightarrow{r} = 2 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j} - 3 \hat{k}\, \text{m}$, the work is $\overrightarrow{F} \cdot \overrightarrow{r} = (3)(2) + (-2)(-3) + (-1)(-3) = 6 + 6 + 3 = 15\, \text{J}$.

Power is the rate of doing work, calculated as $P = \frac{W}{t}$. With $W = 15\, \text{J}$ and $t = 2\, \text{s}$, power is $\frac{15}{2} = 7.5\, \text{W}$.

Option B corresponds to these values.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A point mass ' $m$ ' attached at one end of a massless, inextensible string of length ' $\ell$ ' performs a vertical circular motion and the string rotates in vertical plane, as shown in the diagram. The increase in the centripetal acceleration of the point mass when it moves from point $A$ to point C is [ $\mathrm{g}=$ acceleration due to gravity.]
questions.solution:
The centripetal acceleration at any point on the circular path of radius $\ell$ is given by $a_c = \frac{v^2}{\ell}$, where $v$ is the speed at that point.

Applying conservation of mechanical energy between point A (height $\ell$ above the reference level at C) and point C:

$\frac{1}{2}mv_A^2 + mg\ell = \frac{1}{2}mv_C^2$

Multiplying through by $\frac{2}{m}$ yields:

$v_A^2 + 2g\ell = v_C^2$

The increase in centripetal acceleration from A to C is:

$\Delta a_c = \frac{v_C^2}{\ell} - \frac{v_A^2}{\ell} = \frac{(v_A^2 + 2g\ell)}{\ell} - \frac{v_A^2}{\ell} = 2g$

Final Answer: $2g$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is displaced from point $\mathrm{P}(3 \mathrm{ m}, 4 \mathrm{ m}, 5 \mathrm{ m})$ to a point $Q(2 m, 3 m, 4 m)$ under a constant force $\vec{F}=(3 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+5 \hat{k}) N$. The work done by the force in this process is
questions.solution:
Work done by a constant force

$\vec{F} \cdot \vec{d}$, where $\vec{d} = \vec{r}_Q - \vec{r}_P$ is the displacement.

Given $\vec{r}_P = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k})\mathrm{m}$ and $\vec{r}_Q = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})\mathrm{m}$, the displacement is

$\vec{d} = (2-3)\hat{i} + (3-4)\hat{j} + (4-5)\hat{k} = (-\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k})\mathrm{m}$.

With $\vec{F} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k})\mathrm{N}$, the work done is

$W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d} = (3)(-1) + (4)(-1) + (5)(-1) = -12 \mathrm{ J}$.

The work done is $-12 \mathrm{ J}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass 1 kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\vec{F}=\left(t \hat{i}+2 t^2 \hat{j}\right) N$, where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are unit vectors along $x$ and $y$ axis. The power developed by above force at time $t=3$ second will be
questions.solution:
Given: Mass $m = 1 \text{ kg}$ and force $\vec{F} = (t \hat{i} + 2t^2 \hat{j}) \text{ N}$. The power developed by the force is $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v}$.

Applying Newton's second law, acceleration is $\vec{a} = \frac{\vec{F}}{m} = t \hat{i} + 2t^2 \hat{j} \text{ m/s}^2$. Since the body starts from rest, velocity is found by integrating acceleration: $\vec{v} = \int (t \hat{i} + 2t^2 \hat{j}) \, dt = \left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right) \hat{i} + \left(\frac{2t^3}{3}\right) \hat{j} \text{ m/s}$.

Power is then calculated as $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = (t \hat{i} + 2t^2 \hat{j}) \cdot \left(\frac{t^2}{2} \hat{i} + \frac{2t^3}{3} \hat{j}\right) = \frac{t^3}{2} + \frac{4t^5}{3}$.

At $t = 3$, $P(3) = \frac{27}{2} + \frac{4 \times 243}{3} = 13.5 + 324 = 337.5 \text{ W}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A simple pendulum oscillates with an angular amplitude $\theta$. If the maximum tension in the string is 4 times the minimum tension then the value of $\theta$ is
questions.solution:
The tension $T$ in the pendulum string at angle $\phi$ is expressed as $T = mg \cos\phi + \frac{mv^2}{L}$. Maximum tension occurs at the bottom (\phi = 0$), applying conservation of energy: $v_\max^2 = 2gL(1 - \cos\theta)$. Substitution yields $T_\max = mg(3 - 2\cos\theta)$.

Minimum tension occurs at the amplitude extreme, $T_\min = mg\cos\theta$, where velocity is zero.

Given $T_\max = 4T_\min$, solve: $3 - 2\cos\theta = 4\cos\theta$.

This simplifies to $3 = 6\cos\theta$, giving \cos\theta = 0.5$.

Therefore, $\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.5)$, corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pendulum bob has a speed $4 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ at its lowest position. The pendulum is 1 m long. When the length of the string makes an angle of $60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ with the vertical, the speed of the bob at that position is (acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \cos 60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=0 \cdot 5$ )
questions.solution:
The speed $v_2$ of the pendulum bob when the string makes an angle of $60^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the vertical can be found using conservation of mechanical energy, taking the lowest position as the reference for potential energy.

At the lowest position, the speed is $v_1 = 4 \, \text{m/s}$, so the total energy is $\frac{1}{2}mv_1^2 = 8m$.

At $\theta = 60^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$, the bob is at a height $h = L(1 - \cos\theta) = 0.5 \, \text{m}$ above the reference level, giving a potential energy of $mgh = 5m$.

By conservation of energy, $\frac{1}{2}mv_1^2 = mgh + \frac{1}{2}mv_2^2$. Cancelling $m$ and multiplying by 2 yields $v_1^2 = 2gh + v_2^2$, so $v_2^2 = v_1^2 - 2gh = 16 - 10 = 6$.

The speed is therefore $v_2 = \sqrt{6} \, \text{m/s}$, corresponding to choice $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone is projected with kinetic energy E, making an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. When it reaches a highest point, its kinetic energy is
questions.solution:
Initial kinetic energy: $E = \frac{1}{2} m v_0^2$

For projection angle $\theta$, the velocity at the highest point retains only the horizontal component: $v_h = v_0 \cos \theta$.

The kinetic energy at this point becomes:

$E_h = \frac{1}{2} m v_h^2 = \frac{1}{2} m (v_0 \cos \theta)^2 = \frac{1}{2} m v_0^2 \cos^2 \theta = E \cos^2 \theta$

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A weightless thread can bear tension up to 3.7 kg wt. A stone of mass 500 gram is tied to it and revolved in circular path of radius 4 m in vertical plane. Maximum angular velocity of the stone will be (acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
Maximum angular velocity occurs at the lowest point where tension is greatest due to the combined effect of weight and centripetal force.

The tension formula at the lowest point is $T = mg + m\omega^2 r$.

Given: $T_{\text\max} = 3.7 \, \text{kg wt} = 37 \, \text{N}$, $m = 0.5 \, \text{kg}$, $r = 4 \, \text{m}$, $g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2$.

Substituting known values:
$37 = 0.5 \times 10 + 0.5 \times \omega^2 \times 4$
$37 = 5 + 2\omega^2$
$32 = 2\omega^2$
$\omega^2 = 16$

The angular velocity is $\omega = 4 \, \text{rad/s}$.

Answer: B

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone of mass 1 kg tied to a light inextensible string of length $\mathrm{L}=\frac{5}{3} \mathrm{~m}$ is rotating in a circular path of radius L in a vertical plane. If the ratio of maximum tension in the string to the minimum tension in the string is 3 , the speed of the stone at the highest point of the circle is ( $\mathrm{g}=$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
The forces acting on the stone at the highest point yield the minimum tension, satisfying $T_{\min} + mg = \frac{mv_H^2}{L}$, where $v_H$ is the speed at the highest point. Rearranging gives $T_{\min} = \frac{mv_H^2}{L} - mg$.

At the lowest point, the centripetal force requires $T_{\max} - mg = \frac{mv_L^2}{L}$, giving $T_{\max} = \frac{mv_L^2}{L} + mg$.

By conservation of mechanical energy, taking the lowest point as zero potential energy, $\frac{1}{2}mv_L^2 = \frac{1}{2}mv_H^2 + 2mgL$. Multiplying by $2/m$ yields $v_L^2 = v_H^2 + 4gL$.

Substituting into the expression for $T_{\max}$:

$T_{\max} = \frac{m(v_H^2 + 4gL)}{L} + mg = \frac{mv_H^2}{L} + 4mg + mg = \frac{mv_H^2}{L} + 5mg$

Given $T_{\max}/T_{\min} = 3$, we substitute the expressions:

$\frac{\frac{mv_H^2}{L} + 5mg}{\frac{mv_H^2}{L} - mg} = 3$

Letting $X = \frac{mv_H^2}{L}$, the equation becomes $\frac{X + 5mg}{X - mg} = 3$, leading to $X + 5mg = 3(X - mg)$. Solving gives $X = 4mg$.

Thus $\frac{mv_H^2}{L} = 4mg$, so $v_H^2 = 4gL$ and $v_H = 2\sqrt{gL}$.

Final speed at highest point: $2\sqrt{gL}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The bob of a pendulum of length ' $l$ ' is pulled aside from its equilibrium position through an angle ' $\theta$ ' and then released. The bob will then pass through its equilibrium position with speed ' $v$ ', where ' $v$ ' equal to ( $g=$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution: When bob of a pendulum rises up a height ' $h$ ' potential energy at extreme position becomes kinetic energy of mean position. $\begin{array}{ll} & \mathrm{mgh}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\max }^2 \\ \therefore \quad & \mathrm{v}_{\max }=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gh}} \\ \quad & l=\mathrm{h}+l \cos \theta \\ \therefore \quad & \mathrm{ h}=l(1-\cos \theta) \\ \therefore \quad & \mathrm{v}_{\max }=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gl}(1-\cos \theta)} \end{array}$

questions.q: A body of mass 1 kg starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration. In 2 seconds, its velocity is $10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. The power exerted on the body in one second is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & P=\frac{W}{t} \\ & W=\text { change in } K E \\ \therefore \quad & W=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}\left(\mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{u}^2\right)=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 10^2=50 \mathrm{ J} \\ \therefore \quad & P=\frac{50}{2}=25 \mathrm{ W}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body moves along a circular path of radius 15 cm. It starts from a point on the circular path and reaches the end of diameter in 3 second. The angular speed of the body in rad $/ \mathrm{s}$ is

questions.q: A particle at rest starts moving with a constant angular acceleration of $4 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^2$ in a circular path. The time at which magnitudes of its centripetal acceleration and tangential acceleration will be equal, is (in second)
questions.solution:
Given that, $\alpha=4 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^2$ Centripetal (radial) acceleration, $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{r}}=\mathrm{r} \omega^2$ Tangential acceleration, $a_t=r \alpha$ If $a_r=a_t$, then $r \omega^2=r \alpha$
$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore \omega^2=$\alpha=$4 \\ \therefore $\omega=\sqrt{4}=$2 $\mathrm{rad}$/ $\mathrm{s}\\ \therefore \text { But, } \omega=\omega_0+$\alpha \mathrm{t}=$0+$\alpha \mathrm{t}=\alpha \mathrm{t}\\ \therefore \text{ and } 2=4 \mathrm{t}\\ \therefore \mathrm{t}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ s} \end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball of mass ' $\mathrm{m}$ ' is dropped from a height ' $\mathrm{s}$ ' on a horizontal platform fixed at the top of a vertical spring. The platform is depressed by a distance ' $h$ '. The spring constant is ( $\mathrm{g}=$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
From the question, it can be understood that the total distance the ball falls is $(\mathrm{S}+\mathrm{h})$
The spring is compressed through a length $h\therefore \quad$ Loss of P.E. by the ball $=\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{S}+\mathrm{h})$
Work done on the spring $=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Kh}^2$
Using law of conservation of energy,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Kh}^2=\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{S}+\mathrm{h}) \\
\therefore \quad & \mathrm{K}=\frac{2 \mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{S}+\mathrm{h})}{\mathrm{h}^2}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone is projected vertically upwards with speed ' $v$ '. Another stone of same mass is projected at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the vertical with the same speed ' $v$ '. The ratio of their potential energies at the highest points of their journey is \left[\sin 30^{\circ}=\cos 60^{\circ}=0.5\right.$,  \left.\cos 30^{\circ}=\sin 60^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right]$
questions.solution:
P.E. of the stone projected vertically is, P.E. = mgh
But $\mathrm{h}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{2 \mathrm{ g}}\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad \text { P. } \mathrm{E}_1 & =\mathrm{mg}\left(\frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{2 \mathrm{ g}}\right) \\
& =\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{2}... (i)
\end{aligned}$
For the second stone thrown at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal,
$\begin{array}{ll} & \mathrm{h}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{ g}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2 \sin ^2 30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}}{2 \mathrm{ g}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{8 \mathrm{ g}} \\
\therefore \quad & \text { P.E. } 2=\mathrm{mg}\left(\frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{8 \mathrm{ g}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{8}... (ii)
\end{array}
Dividing equation (i) by equation (ii) -
$-$\frac{P \cdot E_1}{P \cdot E_2}=\frac{\left(\frac{m v^2}{2}\right)}{\left(\frac{m v^2}{8}\right)}=$4: 1

questions.q: When a long spring of $4 \mathrm{ cm}$ is stretched by $1 \mathrm{ cm}$, the potential energy stored in the spring is $U$. If it is stretched by $4 \mathrm{ cm}$, the potential energy stored in it is
questions.solution:
The potential energy $U$ relates to an extension $x$ via,
$\begin{aligned} & U=\frac{1}{2} K x^2 \\ & \therefore \frac{U^{\prime}}{U}=\frac{x^{\prime 2}}{x^2}=\frac{4^2}{1^2}=16\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A string of $L$ is fixed at one end and carries a mass $M$ at the other end. The string makes $\frac{\pi}{2}$ revolutions per second around the vertical axis through the fixed end as shown in the figure, then the tension in the string is
questions.solution:
Given: $\omega=\frac{2}{\pi}$ rev.per sec
$\Rightarrow \omega=2 \pi \frac{2}{\pi} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}=4 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
The horizontal force balance reads:
$T \sin \theta=M R \omega^2$
From figure $R=L \sin \theta\Rightarrow T=M L \omega^2$
On introducing, $\omega=4 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}\Rightarrow T=M L(4)^2=16 \mathrm{ML}$

questions.q: A string of length ' $L$ ' fixed at one end carries a mass ' $m$ ' at the other end. The string makes $\frac{3}{\pi}$ r.p.s. around the vertical axis through fixed end. The tension in the string is
questions.solution:
Consider the free body diagram
On considering horizontal force balance: $\mathrm{T} \sin \theta=\mathrm{m} \omega^2 \mathrm{R}$ Using the geometry, $\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{L} \sin \theta\therefore \mathrm{T}= \left(\mathrm{m} \omega^2 \mathrm{~L}\right)$ Given, $\omega= \left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)$ r.p.s. $=\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)(2 \pi) \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}=6 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}\therefore \mathrm{T}=36 \mathrm{~mL}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A weightless string can support a tension up to $30 \mathrm{ N}$. A stone of mass $0.5 \mathrm{ kg}$ is tied to its one end and is revolved in a circular path of radius $2 \mathrm{ m}$ in a vertical plane. Then the maximum angular velocity of the stone will be (acceleration due to gravity $g=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
Considering force balance:
$\begin{aligned} & T_{\max }=m \omega_{\max }^2 r+m g \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{T_{\text {max }}}{m}=\omega_{\max }^2 r+g \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{30 \mathrm{ N}}{0.5 \mathrm{ kg}}-10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2=\omega_{\max }^2 r \\ & \Rightarrow \omega_{\max }=\sqrt{\frac{50}{2}}=5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A gardener pushes a lawn roller through a distance $20 \mathrm{ m}$. If he applies a force of $30 \mathrm{ kg}-\mathrm{wt}$ in a direction inclined at $60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ to the ground, the work done by the gardener in pushing the roller is \left[\mathrm{g}=$9.8 \mathrm{ m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2, \sin 30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\cos 60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=$\frac{1}{2}, \cos$30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\sin 60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $4 \mathrm{ kg}$ mass and a $1 \mathrm{ kg}$ mass are moving with equal energies. The ratio of the magnitude of their linear momenta is
questions.solution:
The correct option is (A).
Kinetic Energy $\mathrm{K}$ and momentum $p$ are related as:
$\mathrm{K}=\frac{\mathrm{p}^2}{2 \mathrm{ m}}$
Therefore,
$P=\sqrt{2 K m}$
The ratio of momentum for $4 \mathrm{ kg}$ mass and $1 \mathrm{ kg}$ mass moving with equal kinetic energy $\mathrm{K}$ is
$\frac{\mathrm{p}_{4 \mathrm{ kg}}}{\mathrm{p}_{1 \mathrm{ kg}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{ K}(4 \mathrm{ m})}{2 \mathrm{ K}(\mathrm{ m})}}=\frac{2}{1}$

questions.q: A sphere of mass 25 gram is placed on a vertical spring. Spring is compressed by $0.2 \mathrm{ m}$ using a force $5 \mathrm{ N}$. When the spring is relaxed, mass is reaching a height of  \left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Gravitational potential energy gained by the ball $=$ Elastic potential energy in the spring $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{mgh}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Fx}\\
& \therefore \mathrm{h}=\frac{\mathrm{Fx}}{2 \mathrm{mg}}\\
& =\frac{5 \times 0.2}{2 \times 25 \times 10^{-3} \times 10}\\
& =2 \mathrm{ m}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The kinetic energy of a light body and a heavy body is same. Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: The light body has greater momentum.
A body having high velocity has greater momentum.
The heavy body has greater momentum.
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy,
$\mathrm{k}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{my}^{2}=\frac{(\mathrm{mv})^{2}}{2 \mathrm{ m}}=\frac{\mathrmp^{2}}{2 \mathrm{ m}}$
or $\mathrm{p}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mk}}$ i.e., $\mathrm{p} \propto=\sqrt{\mathrm{m}}$
Thus the heavier body has a greater momentum than the lighter one.

questions.q: A body slides down a smooth inclined plane having angle ' $\theta$ ' and reaches the bottom with velocity 'v'. If a body is a sphere then its linear velocity at the bottom of the plane is
questions.solution:
The linear velocity of the body, $v=\sqrt{2 g h}$
The velocity of the sphere about its centre,
$v_{C M}=\sqrt{\frac{2 g h}{1+\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}}}=\frac{v}{\sqrt{1+\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}}} \ldots(\text { i })$
For uniform solid sphere,
$\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}=\frac{2}{5}$
Substituting value in Eq. (i), we get
$v_{C M}=\frac{v}{\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{7} v}$

Two masses of 1 gram and 4 gram are moving with equal kinetic energy. The ratio
of the magnitudes of their momenta is
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy $\mathrm{K}=\frac{\mathrmp^{2}}{2 \mathrm{ m}}$
Two masses are given as- $\mathrm{m}_{1}=1 \mathrm{gm}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{2}=4 \mathrm{gm}$
But $\mathrm{K}_{1}=\mathrm{K}_{2}\therefore \frac{\mathrm{p}_{1}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{ m}_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{ m}_{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long spring is stretched by $2 \mathrm{ cm}$ and its potential energy is $U$. If the spring is stretched by $10 \mathrm{ cm}$; its potential energy will be
questions.solution:
The potential energy of a stretched spring is U=$\frac{1}{2}$ k x^{2} Here, $k=$ spring constant, $x=$ elongation in spring. But given that, the elongation is $2 \mathrm{ cm}$.
So, $U=\frac{1}{2} k(2)^{2}
\Rightarrow \quad U=\frac{1}{2}$ k $\times$4...(i) If elongation is $10 \mathrm{ cm}$ then potential energy $\begin{aligned}$ U^{\prime} &=$\frac{1}{2}$ k(10)^{2} \\
U^{\prime} &=$\frac{1}{2}$ k $\times$100...(ii)
\end{aligned} On dividing Eq. (ii) by Eq. (i), we have $\frac{U^{\prime}}{U}=\frac{\frac{1}{2} k \times 100}{\frac{1}{2} k \times 4}$ or $\frac{U^{\prime}}{U}=25 \Rightarrow U^{\prime}=25 U$
